notes.meaning: God promises a flowing spring of water to wash away the sins and moral uncleanness of His people. This points forward to the forgiveness found in Christ, whose sacrifice removes the guilt of sin. The fountain stands wide open for anyone who repents and comes to Him for spiritual cleansing.

God announces that He will wipe out every trace of idol worship so completely that the false gods will never be mentioned again. He also promises to remove all false prophets and the evil spirits that mislead the people. When God cleanses His people, He removes both the guilt of sin and the things that lead them into it.

Love for God and His truth will become so strong that it overrides even the closest family ties. If a person tries to spread lies in God's name, their own father and mother will carry out the law against false prophets. God's people will care more about honoring Him than protecting wrongdoing within their own families.

Those who previously pretended to receive visions from God will feel deeply ashamed of their lies. Prophets in ancient times often wore rough garments made of animal hair, but false teachers will no longer put on these cloaks to look holy. Deceit will lose its power to trick the community.

Exposed deceivers will quickly deny that they ever claimed to be prophets. Instead, a former false teacher will claim to be just an ordinary farm worker who has tilled the soil from youth. The fear of being caught will drive people to turn away from religious deception and accept honest labor.

When an accused deceiver is asked about scars on his body, he will make up an excuse to hide his past. Pagan prophets often slashed themselves during idol worship to get their gods' attention, but this person claims he was merely injured at a friend's home. People will go to great lengths to hide their past unfaithfulness to God.

differ.view: Some read this as a picture of Christ, where the Savior speaks of the nail marks from His crucifixion received among His own people.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Many readers and preachers understand these wounds as a prophetic picture of Jesus being pierced on the cross by His own people.

notes.meaning: God calls for a sword of judgment to strike His chosen Shepherd, who is described as His close companion and equal. When the Shepherd is struck down, His flock will scatter, yet God promises to care for the weak and humble disciples. Jesus quoted this passage on the night He was arrested to show that His suffering was part of God's plan to save His people.

A terrible time of judgment will sweep through the land, causing two-thirds of the population to perish. Yet God promises to preserve a remnant, a surviving portion of one-third. Even when judgment falls, the Lord always protects those He intends to save.

God will lead the surviving one-third through great suffering to purify their faith, just as a metalsmith uses fire to remove impurities from silver and gold. When they call out to the Lord in prayer, He will hear them and restore their covenant bond. He will claim them as His own people, and they will gladly claim Him as their God.
